note — the bold part is what the card te: The modals lose their umlaut in the past and add -te: können → konnte. ich and er have no extra ending.
müssen → musste: no umlaut. In speech, the modals are used in this simple past, not the perfect.

English: We **had to** wait a long time.

note — the bold part is what the card te: ich musste; the infinitive aufstehen at the end, in one word.
The modal second, the infinitive last.

English: As a child I **wasn't allowed** to watch TV.
We **were supposed to** bring a cake.

note — the bold part is what the card te: Regular verbs add -te to the stem: sagte. Stories and news use this simple past.

English: Once upon a time there **was** a king.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Every fairy tale starts this way: Es war einmal…
Irregular verbs change their vowel and add no -te: gehen → ging.
kommen → kam. plötzlich first, kam second.

English: The queen **was sitting** in the castle.
The animal **was standing** in the garden.

note — the bold part is what the card te: wissen is mixed: a new stem and -te, wusste.

English: I **thought** that you were coming today. (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: denken → dachte, mixed like bringen → brachte.

English: He **drank** a coffee and left at once.
German: Er **trank** einen Kaffee und ging sofort.
